rationale.usefulness: Frozen tutoring moments, paired prompt conditions, reference conversations and a documented runner provide directly useful diagnostics for educational builders. The report connects these to hint-policy regression checks, teacher review and explanatory media while carefully separating benchmark behavior from learner benefit.
rationale.impact: Context-sensitive intervention evaluation is a meaningful advance for educational AI development beyond answer correctness. Its single-program math scope, synthetic student and noisy scoring prevent extrapolation to field-wide significance or proven learning improvements.
rationale.novelty: Evaluating when to scaffold versus require rigor at teacher-selected decision points is a distinctive and well-motivated benchmark design. Frozen personas and replay comparisons add value beyond generic tutor rankings, though synthetic evaluation and model judging remain established techniques.
rationale.maturity: A documented Python runner, revision/hash provenance, failure accounting and released reference data support reproducible new experiments. The original human action classifications are unavailable, parts of scoring are noisy, and real-student validation is absent, so readiness remains bounded.
rationale.openness: Apache code, CC BY data, prompts, frozen moments, reference replays and explicit provenance provide strong inspection and reuse. Lost classifications prevent reproduction of particular paper analyses; third-party model terms and hosted replay dependencies keep the release below exceptional full reproducibility.

concerns: The missing original human action classifications affect KL/action-distribution reproduction, not the existence of runnable moments; the report maintains that distinction.
Historical author-reported rigor figures are verified against the archived blog and appropriately excluded from current-model or learning-effect claims.
Real-student efficacy, wider curriculum generalization and imperfect de-identification remain explicit limitations.
